hot.title: Autodata: An agentic data scientist to create high quality synthetic data
hot.summary: Autodata introduces an agentic framework for autonomously generating and curating high-quality synthetic data to train large language models (LLMs). Through iterative feedback and meta-optimization of the data generation process, it produces data that optimally challenges target models, leading to performance improvements of up to 13.2% in CS research tasks and 17.0% in legal reasoning tasks, while enhancing reasoning efficiency in mathematical problems.

hot.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents
hot.summary: Qwen-AgentWorld introduces a family of language world models (LWMs) that simulate diverse agentic environments, surpassing frontier LLMs on the AgentWorldBench and improving agent performance across various downstream tasks. These models enhance agent learning through scalable, controllable simulation and by integrating internal predictive reasoning for action refinement.

hot.title: Previewing GPT‑5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
Scaling Laws, Carefully
Wan-Streamer v0.1: End-to-end Real-time Interactive Foundation Models
hot.summary: The Wan Team at Alibaba Group developed Wan-Streamer v0.1, an end-to-end streaming foundation model for full-duplex multimodal interaction, integrating language, audio, and video. It demonstrates a model-side response latency of 200 ms and a total interaction latency of 550 ms, supporting real-time, natural human-AI communication with continuous visual presence and dynamic turn-taking.

hot.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
hot.summary: This research systematically evaluates existing large language model agent memory systems from a data management perspective, introducing a four-module analytical framework and conducting extensive empirical studies across 12 architectures and five benchmark workloads. The study provides insights into architectural trade-offs, operational costs, and how different memory components impact task effectiveness, retrieval fidelity, and dynamic update robustness.

hot.title: Accelerating Gemini Nano models on Pixel with frozen Multi-Token Prediction
DanceOPD: On-Policy Generative Field Distillation
hot.summary: DanceOPD is an on-policy generative field distillation framework that enables a single flow-matching model to effectively compose diverse capabilities like text-to-image generation and various image editing tasks. The framework consistently improves target capabilities, such as editing scores by up to 21.9% in specific categories, while preserving or enhancing anchor generation quality by up to 2.0% in T2I metrics.

hot.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models
hot.summary: This research systematically investigates and establishes an open data curation pipeline for training broadly capable agentic language models, identifying effective strategies for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data and demonstrating its efficacy with a new dataset that improves agentic model performance. The study also explores reinforcement learning (RL) data curation, finding that specific RL data sources can induce exploratory agent behaviors and further enhance capabilities when combined with SFT.

hot.title: Qwen-Image-Agent: Bridging the Context Gap in Real-World Image Generation
hot.summary: Qwen-Image-Agent is introduced as an end-to-end framework from the Qwen team, designed to bridge the "Context Gap" in real-world image generation by integrating planning, reasoning, search, memory, and feedback. The framework establishes state-of-the-art performance on the newly proposed IA-Bench benchmark with an IA-score of 45.4%, and also achieves top results on WISE-Verified (0.9020) and MindBench (0.42), demonstrating its ability to handle underspecified and knowledge-dependent requests.

hot.title: Improved Large Language Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Researchers at Renmin University of China and ByteDance developed iLLaDA, an 8-billion parameter fully bidirectional masked diffusion language model, achieving performance competitive with leading autoregressive models and substantial improvements over prior diffusion LLMs across various benchmarks.

hot.title: You Don't Need to Run Every Eval
hot.summary: Microsoft Research developed BENCHPRESS, a system leveraging the observed rank-2 structure of LLM benchmark scores to predict a model's full performance profile from a small subset of evaluations. The system achieves a median absolute error of 4.6 score points on unseen data and can recover model rankings with 92.1% accuracy, significantly reducing evaluation costs.

hot.title: Fast LeWorldModel
hot.summary: Fast-LeWM introduces an action-prefix prediction method for visual world models, enabling parallel forecasting of future latent states. This approach achieves a 3.9x acceleration in dynamics evaluation and a 48% reduction in total planning time while improving planning success rates to 90.5% on average and mitigating error accumulation in long-horizon predictions.

hot.title: World Value Models for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: This research introduces the World Value Model (WVM), which repurposes spatiotemporal priors from video world models to achieve a generalist robotic value estimator with enhanced temporal understanding. It establishes a new evaluation benchmark, Suboptimal-Value-Bench, demonstrating WVM's superior ability to track task progress in suboptimal scenarios and guide robust policy learning from mixed-quality data.

hot.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match the Published SOTA of Nature-Family Papers?
hot.summary: This work introduces NatureBench, a benchmark and automated pipeline (NatureGym), to evaluate AI coding agents' ability to surpass published scientific state-of-the-art (SOTA) across 90 tasks derived from Nature-family papers. It finds that current frontier agents achieve limited SOTA surpassing (max 17.8% of tasks) and moderate SOTA matching (max 47.8%), relying primarily on generic ML engineering rather than novel scientific discovery.

hot.title: Improving Neural Network Training by Decoupling the Magnitude and Direction of Weight Vectors
hot.summary: Researchers at EPFL's Machine Learning and Optimization Lab developed Magnitude–Direction (MD) Decoupling, an optimizer modification that separates the learning dynamics of weight vector magnitudes and directions. This approach consistently improved performance, eliminated the need for weight decay and learning rate warmup, facilitated learning rate transfer across model sizes, and reduced compute requirements by approximately 2x for large Mixture-of-Experts models.

hot.title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: OPID (On-Policy Skill Distillation) introduces a framework that enhances large language model (LLM) agents by extracting hierarchical, natural-language skills directly from their completed on-policy trajectories. This method consistently improves agent performance across embodied reasoning, web navigation, and search-based QA tasks, demonstrating up to a 26.5 point increase in success rate on WebShop for smaller LLMs and better sample efficiency compared to outcome-only reinforcement learning.

hot.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI: From Foundations to Systems
hot.summary: Haggai Roitman's guide synthesizes the fragmented knowledge spanning LLM foundations, reinforcement learning, systems engineering, and agentic architectures into a unified, practical reference. It provides a comprehensive overview of established methodologies and architectural patterns to equip practitioners with the understanding needed to construct and deploy advanced AI systems.

hot.title: LA4VLA: Learning to Act without Seeing via Language-Action Pretraining
hot.summary: LA4VLA introduces a pretraining framework that decouples language-action learning from visual grounding to develop robust, vision-independent action priors for robot policies. This approach, which includes the LA4-33K dataset and various pretraining paradigms, improves manipulation performance by up to 45.0 percentage points in real-world tasks and enhances robustness to visual perturbations.

hot.title: Tmax: A simple recipe for terminal agents
hot.summary: Researchers at the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington developed TMAX-15K, a large and diverse dataset of complex terminal tasks, alongside a simple reinforcement learning (RL) training recipe for open-weight language models. This approach enabled TMAX-9B to achieve 27.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, making it the top-performing open-weight model under 10 billion parameters at the time of publication and surpassing several larger models.

likes.title: Unlimited OCR Works
likes.summary: Unlimited OCR introduces a model for one-shot, long-horizon parsing of multi-page documents, employing a Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) mechanism to maintain a constant KV cache size and stable inference speed. The model achieved an overall score of 93.23% on OmniDocBench v1.5, representing a 6.22 percentage point improvement over its baseline, while efficiently processing continuous document streams.

likes.title: Tapered Language Models
likes.summary: This work introduces Tapered Language Models (TLMs), an architectural principle that monotonically decreases a parameter-bearing component's capacity, specifically MLP width, across model depth while maintaining a fixed total parameter budget. The approach consistently improved average commonsense reasoning accuracy and perplexity across diverse architectures and scales, achieving up to 1.84 perplexity points improvement on a 440M Transformer compared to uniform baselines.

likes.title: Agent-as-a-Router: Agentic Model Routing for Coding Tasks
likes.summary: The Agent-as-a-Router framework, instantiated as ACRouter, introduces a dynamic, self-adaptive model routing paradigm for coding tasks, continuously learning from execution-grounded feedback to select optimal Large Language Models. This approach achieves the lowest cumulative regret and improved cost-efficiency on a new benchmark, CodeRouterBench, demonstrating strong generalization to out-of-distribution agentic programming tasks.

likes.title: Scaling Laws, Carefully
ParallelKernelBench: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels?
likes.summary: ParallelKernelBench (PKB), a new benchmark and evaluation framework, assesses the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate high-performance multi-GPU kernels. The evaluation shows frontier LLMs struggle with complex distributed parallelism, achieving limited correctness and speedup in single-shot settings, though they occasionally produce 'net new' kernels that outperform PyTorch+NCCL baselines for specific workloads.

likes.title: MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?
likes.summary: A new benchmark, MAS-PromptBench, systematically quantifies the effects of prompt optimization in multi-agent LLM systems, revealing that while optimization can improve performance by up to 24.0 percentage points in specific setups, it can also cause degradations of up to 16.0 points, with outcomes heavily influenced by task type, communication structure, and team size.

likes.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
likes.summary: INSIGHT introduces a framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to autonomously acquire new manipulation skills by identifying missing primitive actions and generating their own training data. The system enables robots to continually expand their learned skill vocabulary, achieving high success rates in novel tasks while retaining prior capabilities and improving execution efficiency.

likes.title: HoloAgent-0: A Unified Embodied Agent Framework with 3D Spatial Memory
likes.summary: HoloAgent-0, a unified embodied agent framework developed by Horizon Robotics and D-Robotics Robotics, bridges the divide between large language model reasoning and real-world physical robot execution. It integrates persistent 3D spatial memory and a structured skill interface to facilitate robust, closed-loop task execution, demonstrating high success rates in real-robot navigation and competitive performance in semantic mapping.

likes.summary: SeFi-Image is a text-to-image foundation model that leverages a Semantic-First Diffusion paradigm to achieve high-quality image generation. The model produces competitive or superior results on benchmarks for prompt following, text rendering, and bilingual generation, notably with substantially reduced training computational cost compared to other leading models.

likes.title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild
likes.summary: Carnegie Mellon University researchers developed Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework that reconstructs complete 4D (3D geometry and motion) representations of dynamic, non-rigid objects from monocular in-the-wild videos. The system integrates causal latent propagation for temporal consistency and occlusion-aware appearance refinement with view-conditioned diffusion priors, demonstrating improved perceptual quality, temporal coherence, and semantic fidelity over prior methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.

likes.title: JAXBench: Benchmarking Autonomous TPU Kernel Optimization
likes.summary: JAXBench introduces a TPU-native benchmark suite to evaluate autonomous kernel optimization methods, featuring 50 JAX workloads derived from production LLMs and providing device-side profiling for accurate measurement. The benchmark demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLM agents can achieve a 1.36x geomean speedup over XLA compilation, reaching about 77% of hand-tuned Pallas kernel performance on specific compute-bound tasks.
